subject: Deckstone dedicated GPU pool: cutover, autoscale & burst governance
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Rajiv Sharma <rajiv@deckstone.com>, Priya Menon <priya.m@deckstone.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Mar 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Deckstone dedicated GPU pool - cutover & burst governance

Tessa / Monica —

Quick summary and handoff: Deckstone signed the Dedicated capacity SOW last week (deal DS-4837). They’re planning a phased cutover for inference traffic starting mid-April. Key asks from Sales/Legal:
- Reserved 16-GPU pool (A100 equivalent) for production in us-west-2, with eu-west-1 as DR.
- Autoscale policy: warm pool + burst to shared capacity for spikes up to 2x baseline.
- Contract requires an SLA measurement during first 30 days and a documented fallback policy.

I’ve attached a first-draft MAP (Deckstone-MAP-v1.xlsx) and capacity estimates (capacity-estimates.csv). Can the CS/Implementations team own the activation plan and confirm timeline? Suggested milestone: kickoff 2029-03-12, staging cutover 2029-04-08, prod cutover 2029-04-15.

Immediate questions for planning:
1) Do we have ops capacity for a same-day canary in us-west-2?
2) Are we comfortable with automatic burst to shared (non-dedicated) on peak, or should we require manual approval for bursts above 1.5x?

Tessa — tagging you to lead the implementation plan. Monica / Karthik — please add operational notes for autoscale and netops dependencies.

Thanks,
Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
attachments: Deckstone-MAP-v1.xlsx, capacity-estimates.csv

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Rajiv Sharma <rajiv@deckstone.com>, Priya Menon <priya.m@deckstone.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Mar 2029 12:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Deckstone dedicated GPU pool - cutover & burst governance

Thanks Ben — I’ll take point on this. I’ll run a kickoff invite for 2029-03-12 and put together a short activation checklist. A few clarifying items before I draft the MAP into our implementation template:

- Can Rajiv confirm expected p95 generation latency target at 1k tokens? (we need this to size queueing/scale guardrails)
- For burst behavior: do they require hard isolation (never to shared) or prefer predictable economic fallback? If they need isolation we’ll need a larger reserved baseline or a pre-approved burst buffer.
- Any region compliance constraints for eu-west-1 as DR? (e.g., data residency for logs)

Monica / Karthik — please advise on:
* Autoscale warm thresholds (we typically recommend maintaining 10–15% warm spare capacity for predictable latency).
* Suggested canary strategy: single-rack warm pool canary in us-west-2, throttling to 20% of total traffic for 24h, then ramp.

I’ll update the MAP and post a Drive link in the next message.

Subject: Re: Deckstone dedicated GPU pool - cutover & burst governance

Thanks Ben & Tessa — quick answers from our side:

- p95 latency: target is <= 350ms at 1k tokens for production; staging can tolerate up to 450ms.
- Burst preference: we’d like predictable fallback to shared only for short bursts (up to 30 minutes). For sustained >1.5x load, we want an alert + manual approval to expand capacity.
- Regions: primary in us-west-2 (we have a customer base concentrated on west coast), DR in eu-west-1 is fine for model weights and failover; however, logs containing PII must remain in-region. We can redact PII prior to logs forwarding if necessary.

We’ve included a simple traffic forecast in the attached CSV (capacity-estimates.csv). Peak predicted concurrency: 210 concurrent requests, typical baseline 90.

Can the team confirm proposed canary throttling (20% traffic) and whether a pre-warm period of 2 hours is required before canary starts?

—Rajiv
Head of Platform | Deckstone Analytics

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Sharma <rajiv@deckstone.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 6 Mar 2029 15:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Deckstone dedicated GPU pool - cutover & burst governance

Thanks Rajiv — all clear and helpful. Updated MAP attached and Drive link below with the implementation checklist and timeline. Proposed next steps:

1) Kickoff meeting 2029-03-12 10:00 PT (calendar invite sent)
2) Prewarm plan: 2-hour warm window before canary traffic starts — we’ll spin up warm loaders and validate KV cache priming.
3) Canary: us-west-2 single-rack, 20% traffic for 24h, monitor p95 & error rate.
4) Burst governance: automatic burst allowed up to 1.25x baseline for short spikes (<=30m). Anything over 1.5x triggers automated alert + manual approval (ops + account team). Between 1.25–1.5x we will allow auto-burst but log and notify.
5) DR strategy: replicate model weights to eu-west-1 with logs redaction for PII; failover runbook linked in Drive.

Checklist (short):
- [ ] NetOps VPN peering confirmed for us-west-2 (netops ticket #NET-721)
- [ ] KMS keys configured (customer-managed recommended)
- [ ] Canary runbook loaded to /drive/Deckstone/Canary-Runbook.md
- [ ] Post-cutover SLA measurement window scheduled (30 days)

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Deckstone-Implementation
HubSpot: https://hubspot.company/deal/DS-4837

If that looks good I’ll mark owners on each checklist item and circulate the final MAP before the kickoff. Quick confirmations: Rajiv/Priya, can you confirm the p95 target and the manual approval gate for bursts >1.5x?

Best,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
